spatial_claims.claim: Points A, C, B, D are collinear with C bisecting AB and BD added beyond B in a straight line
AD is a straight line cut at point B (B lies between A and D)
AB is bisected at C with BD added in a straight line, so AD = AC + CB + BD and DB = BD
AC = CB since AB is bisected at C
AB is cut at C (C lies between A and B)

configuration_map: All points lie on a single straight line in the order A-C-B-D. C is the midpoint of segment AB. BD is the added segment beyond B. The proof introduces no auxiliary points or constructions off this line. CD = CB + BD (since C, B, D are collinear in that order). All applications of Book 2 propositions (2.4, 2.6, 2.7) reference segments within this single collinear arrangement and their preconditions (bisection at C for 2.6; cutting at B for 2.7; cutting at C for 2.4) are all satisfied by the given configuration.
pass_reason: The proof is entirely algebraic, applying Book 2 identities (2.4, 2.6, 2.7) to segments on a single straight line A-C-B-D. The only spatial claims are the collinear arrangement and betweenness relations that come directly from the given hypothesis. No novel geometric constructions are introduced, no angle claims are made, and no inside/outside relationships arise. All applications of earlier propositions have their preconditions trivially satisfied by the given collinear configuration. There is no possibility of spatial contradiction.
